The tooling identifies itself as Cairn , an open-source AI penetration-testing framework : it staged the package at /tmp/cairn_pkg and sent a CAIRN_ESRP_PROBE2 connectivity probe. Before publishing, the attacker ran the stealer on their own machine. That run captured an AI coding agent configuration that appears to be the open-source Pi harness backed by a GLM-family model ( pi_glm53 ), routed through a local proxy.
Earlier this year, another Microsoft Python package, durabletask , was compromised after its PyPI token was stolen. We have not linked the two incidents.
agent_framework_meta.pth contains one line: import agent_framework_meta

In 1.26.1, agent_framework_meta/__init__.py then calls _telemetry._start() . The stealer forks into a detached session ( os.setsid()) , or falls back to a daemon thread where fork isn't available. It sets _AF_TEL=1 to avoid running again in child processes.
The file and function names ( _telemetry , "Lightweight runtime diagnostics hook", user-agent af-runtime-diagnostics/1 ) are made to look like legitimate SDK telemetry.
The stealer is focused on Azure and Azure DevOps. It collects:
Environment variables with names containing strings such as TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD, KEY, AZURE, AWS, GITHUB, OPENAI, HF_, FOUNDRY, NPM, PIP, NUGET, SYSTEM, BUILD, AGENT
Other processes' environments : secret-looking values read from up to 300 /proc/*/environ files
.npmrc, pip.conf, .netrc, .git-credentials, .docker/config.json
1.26.2 was uploaded at 21:08 UTC, 33 minutes after 1.26.1. It is a repacked 1.26.1 that sends to the same webhook.site URL, with these changes:

New trigger. agent_framework_meta/__init__.py is restored to the clean 1.26.0 file. Instead, a new top-level af_runtime_diag.pth imports a new top-level module, af_runtime_diag.py , which starts the stealer as soon as it is imported. Searching only for the 1.26.1 file names will miss this version.
We have confirmed the attackers token was on the free tier, and a maximum of 50 requests were captured. However, those requests can contain working cloud, CI and registry credentials.
Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intelligence Center advisory on this incident.
Identify exposure: search lockfiles, CI logs, virtualenvs and container images for agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2. Pin to 1.26.0.

Check for execution : look in site-packages for agent_framework_meta.pth and agent_framework_meta/_telemetry.py (1.26.1), or af_runtime_diag.pth and af_runtime_diag.py (1.26.2). Any Python process started in that environment ran the payload.
Check egress: search proxy and DNS logs for webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb . A 200 means that host's data was accepted. A 410/429 suggests it was rejected.
Rotate credentials on affected hosts and runners:
Azure CLI sessions, Azure DevOps PATs and service connections, npm/PyPI/NuGet/Docker/Hugging Face tokens, git credentials

Audit Azure identities: review sign-in and activity logs for managed identities and federated credentials (workload identity federation) that were reachable from affected VMs, App Services, AKS nodes or ADO pipelines. Stolen managed-identity and OIDC-exchanged tokens are valid for up to 24 hours.

extraction.body: Threat actors have compromised Microsoft's agent-framework package to push a credential stealer, according to reports from Aikido , Chainguard , Endor Labs , OX Security , SafeDep , Socket , StepSecurity , and Google-owned Wiz . The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published 33 minutes apart on November 17, 2026, and are designed to run a credential stealer on every Python start. As of writing, both the release versions have been quarantined on the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository. It's unclear how the attacker managed to obtain publishing access. Agent-framework is the meta-package for Microsoft Agent Framework, an open-source framework for building and orchestrating artificial intelligence (AI) agents using Python. "Both versions install Python startup hooks that silently collect credentials, environment data, and cloud identity tokens, then exfiltrate them to a webhook[.]site endpoint," Socket said in a report. Once either of the versions is installed, the package drops a .pth file in the site-packages root directory, which then gets executed automatically on every interpreter start, causing the credential stealer to run whenever Python is started in an environment, even if the package is not explicitly imported. "Each wheel adds a .pth file to site-packages," Endor Labs said. "Python executes import lines in .pth files on every interpreter start, so the stealer runs on any Python launch in an affected environment, including pip itself, whether or not anything imports Agent Framework." The "agent_framework_meta.pth" file contains a single import statement referencing "agent_framework_meta," which then launches the stealer payload. It's capable of capturing the following data - "Besides reading credentials already on disk, the code asks the platform to issue new ones," SafeDep said. "Rotating stored secrets does not cover those." "In an Azure DevOps pipeline, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN and SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI are enough to request a federated token for api://AzureADTokenExchange. On Azure compute, it asks the managed identity endpoint for an access token to each of these resources. It uses IDENTITY_ENDPOINT or MSI_ENDPOINT on App Service and Functions, and 169.254.169[.]254 elsewhere. It also pulls instance metadata." It's worth noting that the Azure instance metadata service ( IMDS ) is a RESTful web service that runs on a local IP address ("169.254.169[.]254"), and provides information about the virtual machine, its region, tags, and the identity token. All the collected information is saved into a JSON document, zlib-compressed, Base64-encoded, and sent via an HTTPS POST request to a hard-coded URL ("webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb"). Version 1.26.2, on the other hand, imports a new top-level module, af_runtime_diag.py, collects GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, and expands the search patterns used for harvesting credential-related environment variables. extraction.body: Grand Theft Auto VI is finally set to make its long-awaited debut after years of anticipation and multiple delays. The latest installment in Rockstar Games’ critically acclaimed action-adventure franchise, one of the best-selling video game series of all time, is scheduled to hit stores and digital platforms at midnight in your local time on Nov. 19.But before millions of gamers around the world pickup their controllers, we're breaking down the top things you should know about one of the most highly anticipated video game releases in years.RELATED: GTA VI preorder window now open for November releasePreorders for the game began this past summer on June 25. But, unfortunately, some gamers will still have to wait longer. GTA 6 so far is only launching on consoles, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Players looking to play on a PS4 or Xbox One will need to upgrade their system. No release date has been announced for the PC at this time, according to Rockstar customer support. Upon the preorder window opening, Rockstar also revealed the price for two versions of the digital game, starting at $79.99 for standard and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition.Customers who preordered the game may have received bonuses with conditions. Certain digital preorders also include a free month of GTA+, which may renew automatically unless canceled.One thing that may come as a surprise to many is that the game will only be available in a digital download format. Customers can go the traditional route of purchasing a physical boxed version, but those will not contain a disc, only just a digital download code instead of a traditional game disc.Rockstar is also allowing players to download the game early. Their latest support guidance says digital preloading began Nov. Before you begin play, you will have to download the game to your system, and that download can be quite lengthy. Gamers may need to delete older games or expand their console storage before launch.After 13 years of anticipation, multiple delays and endless speculation, GTA 6 is finally here. Their journey intertwines romance, robberies, betrayal and, of course, grand theft auto.The game does feature single-player and multiplayer game modes. However, the multiplayer will not be available at launch. Rockstar describes GTA 6 as a single-player experience. The online multiplayer mode is expected later, but a firm launch date has not been announced.As a trailblazer helping redefine open-world gaming, Grand Theft Auto 6 features freedom to explore from cities, to beaches to swamps and everything in between. The game offers an expanded freedom with cinematic storytelling and detailed worlds that reaches beyond the game's namesake of stealing cars. Grand Theft Auto has long been one of the video game industry's most controversial franchises, drawing criticism over its depictions of violence, criminal activity and sexual content.The latest installment continues that tradition. Grand Theft Auto VI has received an M (Mature 17+) rating from the Entertainment Software Rating Board, meaning the game is intended for players ages 17 and older.According to the ESRB, the game contains intense violence, blood and gore, strong language, nudity, sexual content and depictions of drug and alcohol use.Previous games in the franchise have featured real-life gang members to bring authenticity to characters and dialogue. That commitment to realism has helped keep fans engaged for years. Despite criticism of its depictions of crime and violence, the series has continued to use advancing technology and meticulous attention to detail to create increasingly immersive worlds, a hallmark of the franchise.Grand Theft Auto has been one of the most anticipated video games of all time. What was normally a pretty regular release schedule from the franchise’s start in 1997, the last game in the series was released 13 years ago with Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online. However, since 2013 rumors persisted of a new game, leaving fans having to wait. RELATED: New 'Grand Theft Auto 6' trailer published early following leaksAnticipation finally peaked in 2022 when Rockstar said the game was "well underway", later giving a 2025 release window. Further delays for a variety of unconfirmed reasons came in May 2025, dating the release for the following May, and yet another delay in November 2025 for a release late in the following year. As with many other pop culture moments, the delayed release even garnered a viral meme whenever a surprise or new product release for anything, it was always said the event happened "before we got GTA 6." "With every game we have released, the goal has been to try and exceed your expectations and Grand Theft Auto VI is no exception," the company said in a statement after their May 2025 delay. "We hope you understand we need this extra time to deliver at the level of quality you expect and deserve."The excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto VI extends well beyond the gaming community, with some analysts predicting the release could have a significant economic impact as millions of Americans prepare to take time off work to play.According to the International Business Times, as many as 1.5 million Americans could call out sick or otherwise take the day off to play the game upon its release. Some estimates say it could cost the U.S. economy $1 billion in a single day, although that projection has not been independently verified.Some members of the U.S. government are preparing for the potential lapse in workforce productivity. As a retention perk, the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion in Fort Stewart, Georgia, is offering soldiers who sign their reenlistment contracts "a special 4 day pass" to give them time off to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6.  The excitement is already translating into major sales. According to Sensor Tower, which tracks gaming sales and digital market trends, estimated preorder revenue has reached $1.18 billion from 12.13 million copies sold as of the morning of Nov. 13.RELATED: Grand Theft Auto 6 already at $1 billion in sales a week before launchBen Domenech, host of the Big Ben Podcast, told Fox News the game had already generated more than half a billion dollars in revenue."Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to be amazing, you’re going to have 25-50 million people playing it within the next couple months," Domenech said.The excitement is especially visible in Miami, the real-world inspiration for the game's fictional Vice City. On Wednesday, the night before the release, the NBA’s Miami Heat will host the Milwaukee Bucks for "A Night in Vice City," a one-night-only themed event celebrating the game’s arrival.But once the final buzzer sounds, fans will only have mere minutes left to wait for the main event: returning to Vice City themselves.No more anticipation, countless rumors and multiple delays. 19 — and for millions of gamers, the wait will finally be over.

extraction.body: See more of our coverage in your search results. When “Grand Theft Auto VI” finally drops this week, professional athletes across the globe will immediately begin stealing cars, running from the cops and causing every manner of virtual mayhem under the Vice City sun. The love affair between pro athletes and video games has been strong for decades now, and the most anticipated game release in over a decade is certain to cause sleep-deprived nights and create mostly friendly competition across locker rooms and clubhouses — even if everybody insists they won’t let it be a distraction from their day jobs. “I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,” Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell said with a grin. Atwell is an avid gamer and a Miami native who has been playing the GTA series since childhood, so the release of this iteration set in a fictional Florida is monumental. He preordered “GTA VI” to appear on his console right at midnight — and he even looked into changing his region setting to New Zealand so he could get the game 21 hours earlier, but ultimately decided it wasn’t worth the hassle. “We’ve been waiting for this one for a long, long time,” Atwell said. “You know it’s going to be a big one.” Pro athletes become avid gamers for obvious reasons: They’re nearly all competition junkies with plenty of money and thousands of hours of free time to game after practices, in road hotels and throughout their offseasons. Athletes from Kyler Murray to Karl-Anthony Towns have amassed large followings on the livestreaming platform Twitch, playing games like the NBA 2K and Madden titles or first-person shooters like “Fortnite” and “Call of Duty” before tens of thousands of viewers. Formula 1 champions Max Verstappen and Lando Norris often seem just as enthusiastic about simulated racing as the real thing. Some athletes even become elite gamers: Lakers superstar Luka Doncic, for instance, was a top-500 player in the tank role on “Overwatch 2” two years ago. But no series dazzles a wider spectrum of the gaming public than GTA — and its long absence from the market only made these athletes hungrier. Rockstar Games released “GTA V” in 2013, when a large chunk of the world’s current pro athletes were adolescents, and the release of “GTA VI” has been tantalizingly delayed for several years. Several weeks ago, Houston Rockets center Steven Adams predicted a seismic disruption to all sports when the game finally arrived. “You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide … GTA is dropping,” Adams said. “So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though. Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.” Whether he was joking or not, Adams nonetheless set off rampant chatter about what the game’s release will mean for athlete and workplace productivity. When asked directly, most high-level athletes say they’re too serious about sports to develop a severe case of GTA Flu. That’s the term coined in 2013 when untold thousands of gamers took days off work to dive headfirst into San Andreas, the game’s fictionalized version of Southern California. Los Angeles Rams left guard Steve Avila doesn’t expect athletes to shirk their primary duties, but he knows the game will still affect plenty of pros in more subtle ways. “I think a lot of athletes are responsible,” Avila said. “But if you could check guys’ sleep scores … I think you’d see that some guys’ hours are going to go way down, for sure.” Avila is a big admirer of Rockstar’s artistic ambitions along with GTA’s famously frenetic gameplay. He had never been to California before he played “Grand Theft Auto,” so he and his friends have been repeatedly surprised in recent years to see the real versions of Los Angeles-area landmarks they already recognized from speeding past them in a stolen car while being chased by virtual cops. The Rams players are among the fortunate few athletes who are on their bye week when the game is released — and Avila is even on injured reserve, although he laughingly insists his rehab work will supersede GTA. Hall’s mother only allowed him to play sports video games, so he has been waiting a decade for the chance to immerse himself in a chapter of the GTA franchise. “Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,” Hall said. “But you’ve got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.” Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker is an inveterate gamer who travels with a gaming laptop and has played “Grand Theft Auto” since before multiplayer options were available. The five-time NBA All-Star loves to “go in there and just be reckless,” he said with a laugh. Like Atwell, Booker has already preordered “GTA VI.” The game is a childhood throwback for younger pros like Anaheim Ducks star Leo Carlsson, who played earlier versions for untold hours as a kid in Sweden. He’ll dive into it when the Ducks return from a road trip — and like many athletes, he’s eagerly anticipating the game’s multiplayer component, which isn’t expected to be available until 2027. “I love playing with teammates,” Carlsson said. “If they dropped (GTA) in the summer, it would probably take over huge time in our life.” “GTA VI” is set in a chimerical Florida called Leonida, which contains Vice City – the franchise’s stand-in for Miami. And the NBA’s Miami Heat are at the epicenter of the release when they hold “A Night in Vice City” on Wednesday. The Heat have topped Kaseya Center with a “Vice City” neon sign as an advertisement for the game, and they’ll wear themed alternate uniforms when they face Milwaukee on a special court. The entire night in downtown Miami will have a GTA theme. “It’s a big thing because growing up as a kid, we all were on ‘Grand Theft Auto,’” Heat forward Bobby Portis said. “It’s been like a buildup, and everybody’s been asking when this was going to come out. Just so happy that we’re here in Miami when it does. Definitely an honor to be able to grace the Vice City and be a part of history.” Heat forward Keshad Johnson said he played the GTA franchise “all my life growing up. It’s been so long since the last one came out. But for there to be a new one and to be a part of it, that’s gonna be fire. That’s gonna be dope. … I’ve seen the jerseys. Elite.”

sources.title: Pro athletes clamor for ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ release — but they insist their day jobs come first - New York Post
passages: When “Grand Theft Auto VI” finally drops this week, professional athletes across the globe will immediately begin stealing cars, running from the cops and causing every manner of virtual mayhem under the Vice City sun.

The love affair between pro athletes and video games has been strong for decades now, and the most anticipated game release in over a decade is certain to cause sleep-deprived nights and create mostly friendly competition across locker rooms and clubhouses — even if everybody insists they won’t let it be a distraction from their day jobs.

Pro athletes become avid gamers for obvious reasons: They’re nearly all competition junkies with plenty of money and thousands of hours of free time to game after practices, in road hotels and throughout their offseasons.

Athletes from Kyler Murray to Karl-Anthony Towns have amassed large followings on the livestreaming platform Twitch, playing games like the NBA 2K and Madden titles or first-person shooters like “Fortnite” and “Call of Duty” before tens of thousands of viewers.

The Rams players are among the fortunate few athletes who are on their bye week when the game is released — and Avila is even on injured reserve, although he laughingly insists his rehab work will supersede GTA.
Whether he was joking or not, Adams nonetheless set off rampant chatter about what the game’s release will mean for athlete and workplace productivity.

extraction.body: See more of our coverage in your search results. When “Grand Theft Auto VI” finally drops this week, professional athletes across the globe will immediately begin stealing cars, running from the cops and causing every manner of virtual mayhem under the Vice City sun. The love affair between pro athletes and video games has been strong for decades now, and the most anticipated game release in over a decade is certain to cause sleep-deprived nights and create mostly friendly competition across locker rooms and clubhouses — even if everybody insists they won’t let it be a distraction from their day jobs. “I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,” Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell said with a grin. Atwell is an avid gamer and a Miami native who has been playing the GTA series since childhood, so the release of this iteration set in a fictional Florida is monumental. He preordered “GTA VI” to appear on his console right at midnight — and he even looked into changing his region setting to New Zealand so he could get the game 21 hours earlier, but ultimately decided it wasn’t worth the hassle. “We’ve been waiting for this one for a long, long time,” Atwell said. “You know it’s going to be a big one.” Pro athletes become avid gamers for obvious reasons: They’re nearly all competition junkies with plenty of money and thousands of hours of free time to game after practices, in road hotels and throughout their offseasons. Athletes from Kyler Murray to Karl-Anthony Towns have amassed large followings on the livestreaming platform Twitch, playing games like the NBA 2K and Madden titles or first-person shooters like “Fortnite” and “Call of Duty” before tens of thousands of viewers. Formula 1 champions Max Verstappen and Lando Norris often seem just as enthusiastic about simulated racing as the real thing. Some athletes even become elite gamers: Lakers superstar Luka Doncic, for instance, was a top-500 player in the tank role on “Overwatch 2” two years ago. But no series dazzles a wider spectrum of the gaming public than GTA — and its long absence from the market only made these athletes hungrier. Rockstar Games released “GTA V” in 2013, when a large chunk of the world’s current pro athletes were adolescents, and the release of “GTA VI” has been tantalizingly delayed for several years. Several weeks ago, Houston Rockets center Steven Adams predicted a seismic disruption to all sports when the game finally arrived. “You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide … GTA is dropping,” Adams said. “So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though. Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.” Whether he was joking or not, Adams nonetheless set off rampant chatter about what the game’s release will mean for athlete and workplace productivity. When asked directly, most high-level athletes say they’re too serious about sports to develop a severe case of GTA Flu. That’s the term coined in 2013 when untold thousands of gamers took days off work to dive headfirst into San Andreas, the game’s fictionalized version of Southern California. Los Angeles Rams left guard Steve Avila doesn’t expect athletes to shirk their primary duties, but he knows the game will still affect plenty of pros in more subtle ways. “I think a lot of athletes are responsible,” Avila said. “But if you could check guys’ sleep scores … I think you’d see that some guys’ hours are going to go way down, for sure.” Avila is a big admirer of Rockstar’s artistic ambitions along with GTA’s famously frenetic gameplay. He had never been to California before he played “Grand Theft Auto,” so he and his friends have been repeatedly surprised in recent years to see the real versions of Los Angeles-area landmarks they already recognized from speeding past them in a stolen car while being chased by virtual cops. The Rams players are among the fortunate few athletes who are on their bye week when the game is released — and Avila is even on injured reserve, although he laughingly insists his rehab work will supersede GTA. Hall’s mother only allowed him to play sports video games, so he has been waiting a decade for the chance to immerse himself in a chapter of the GTA franchise. “Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,” Hall said. “But you’ve got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.” Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker is an inveterate gamer who travels with a gaming laptop and has played “Grand Theft Auto” since before multiplayer options were available. The five-time NBA All-Star loves to “go in there and just be reckless,” he said with a laugh. Like Atwell, Booker has already preordered “GTA VI.” The game is a childhood throwback for younger pros like Anaheim Ducks star Leo Carlsson, who played earlier versions for untold hours as a kid in Sweden. He’ll dive into it when the Ducks return from a road trip — and like many athletes, he’s eagerly anticipating the game’s multiplayer component, which isn’t expected to be available until 2027. “I love playing with teammates,” Carlsson said. “If they dropped (GTA) in the summer, it would probably take over huge time in our life.” “GTA VI” is set in a chimerical Florida called Leonida, which contains Vice City – the franchise’s stand-in for Miami. And the NBA’s Miami Heat are at the epicenter of the release when they hold “A Night in Vice City” on Wednesday. The Heat have topped Kaseya Center with a “Vice City” neon sign as an advertisement for the game, and they’ll wear themed alternate uniforms when they face Milwaukee on a special court. The entire night in downtown Miami will have a GTA theme. “It’s a big thing because growing up as a kid, we all were on ‘Grand Theft Auto,’” Heat forward Bobby Portis said. “It’s been like a buildup, and everybody’s been asking when this was going to come out. Just so happy that we’re here in Miami when it does. Definitely an honor to be able to grace the Vice City and be a part of history.” Heat forward Keshad Johnson said he played the GTA franchise “all my life growing up. It’s been so long since the last one came out. But for there to be a new one and to be a part of it, that’s gonna be fire. That’s gonna be dope. … I’ve seen the jerseys. Elite.”

“It’s a big thing because growing up as a kid, we all were on ‘Grand Theft Auto,’” Heat forward Bobby Portis said. “It’s been like a buildup, and everybody’s been asking when this was going to come out. Just so happy that we’re here in Miami when it does. Definitely an honor to be able to grace the Vice City and be a part of history.”

Heat forward Keshad Johnson said he played the GTA franchise “all my life growing up. It’s been so long since the last one came out. But for there to be a new one and to be a part of it, that’s gonna be fire. That’s gonna be dope. … I’ve seen the jerseys. Elite.”

relevantPassages.text: When “Grand Theft Auto VI” finally drops this week, professional athletes across the globe will immediately begin stealing cars, running from the cops and causing every manner of virtual mayhem under the Vice City sun.

The love affair between pro athletes and video games has been strong for decades now, and the most anticipated game release in over a decade is certain to cause sleep-deprived nights and create mostly friendly competition across locker rooms and clubhouses — even if everybody insists they won’t let it be a distraction from their day jobs.

Pro athletes become avid gamers for obvious reasons: They’re nearly all competition junkies with plenty of money and thousands of hours of free time to game after practices, in road hotels and throughout their offseasons.

Athletes from Kyler Murray to Karl-Anthony Towns have amassed large followings on the livestreaming platform Twitch, playing games like the NBA 2K and Madden titles or first-person shooters like “Fortnite” and “Call of Duty” before tens of thousands of viewers.

The Rams players are among the fortunate few athletes who are on their bye week when the game is released — and Avila is even on injured reserve, although he laughingly insists his rehab work will supersede GTA.
Whether he was joking or not, Adams nonetheless set off rampant chatter about what the game’s release will mean for athlete and workplace productivity.

sources.title: Google expands Gemini Tasks, letting users make calls, compare prices and complete payments automatically
passages: Powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Tasks lets you hand off everyday life admin directly: - Forward emails to gemini@google.com to RSVP and add it to your family calendar - Have Gemini call local businesses to compare price quotes and check inventory (with full transcripts + approval before dialing) - Check out securely via Google Pay (uses the Agent Payments Protocol - AP2) - Seamlessly sign in via Google Password Manager We wanted to make this helpful + secure, we’re also partnering directly with major websites and security providers so it works well for site owners and agents. — Sundar Pichai (@sundarpichai) November 17, 2026 Users can also use the agent to schedule emails and manage a range of Google Workspace activities, including Docs, Gmail and the rest of the office suite that many people already use.
Data protection Google says Gemini uses a multi-layered security approach when carrying out tasks through its agentic capabilities.
Google has made Gemini's task features free for users across six countries, including the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia and India.
Announcing the new features, Google added that the update is designed for people whose to-do lists grow during classes, meetings and other tasks.
These features can help users place calls to businesses, process payments and send texts over RCS, the upgraded messaging standard that replaces old-school SMS on many phones.
Knowing things → doing things → finding ways to save you time and money We’re expanding Tasks in Gemini free of charge to hundreds of millions of people in six countries.
These new add-ons are intended to help users streamline their daily activities and keep track of their tasks.

Additional safeguards include prompt-injection filters that scan webpages and search results, Google Safe Browsing to restrict access to potentially harmful links, and human approval checks before sensitive actions, such as making purchases.

sources.title: Google expands Gemini Tasks to millions of users, adds calling and shopping features
passages: Google has announced a major expansion of Gemini Tasks, its AI-powered assistant feature that can perform multi-step actions on behalf of users, including calling businesses, comparing prices and helping complete purchases.

Google says the AI can contact local businesses, compare services, check inventory, confirm pricing and even schedule appointments.Google executive Josh Woodward cited an example in which Gemini contacted multiple vehicle dealerships, checked appointment availability and coordinated scheduling through the user's calendar.Shopping and Google Pay integrationGoogle is also expanding shopping capabilities within Gemini Tasks.

The company also emphasised that major actions, including purchases and bookings, require user confirmation before being completed.The expanded rollout comes as major technology companies race to build AI agents capable of handling real-world tasks, with Google positioning Gemini as an assistant that can not only provide information but also help users get things done.Your child uses AI every day.
The company is now rolling out the feature free of charge to hundreds of millions of users in six countries, including India, the US, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea.
Users can ask the AI assistant to create travel itineraries, analyse information from emails, prepare daily briefings using calendar data, automate research tasks and organise schedules.
Once Gemini finds a matching product, it can prepare the checkout process using Google Pay.
Users can send instructions through text messages, while US users can also forward emails directly to Gemini for actions such as extracting dates and adding events to calendars.

sources.title: Google expands Gemini Tasks to millions of users, adds calling and shopping features
passages: Google has announced a major expansion of Gemini Tasks, its AI-powered assistant feature that can perform multi-step actions on behalf of users, including calling businesses, comparing prices and helping complete purchases.

Google says the AI can contact local businesses, compare services, check inventory, confirm pricing and even schedule appointments.Google executive Josh Woodward cited an example in which Gemini contacted multiple vehicle dealerships, checked appointment availability and coordinated scheduling through the user's calendar.Shopping and Google Pay integrationGoogle is also expanding shopping capabilities within Gemini Tasks.

The company also emphasised that major actions, including purchases and bookings, require user confirmation before being completed.The expanded rollout comes as major technology companies race to build AI agents capable of handling real-world tasks, with Google positioning Gemini as an assistant that can not only provide information but also help users get things done.Your child uses AI every day.
The company is now rolling out the feature free of charge to hundreds of millions of users in six countries, including India, the US, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea.
Users can ask the AI assistant to create travel itineraries, analyse information from emails, prepare daily briefings using calendar data, automate research tasks and organise schedules.
Once Gemini finds a matching product, it can prepare the checkout process using Google Pay.
Users can send instructions through text messages, while US users can also forward emails directly to Gemini for actions such as extracting dates and adding events to calendars.

Huang also acknowledged his personal misconduct and pledged to cooperate with an independent investigation commissioned by Nvidia’s directors. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” he said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. Nvidia has named longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent replacement for Huang. President Trump weighed in Monday, saying he would support Huang’s return to the helm of the AI chipmaking giant. Musk has also backed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement, joining other prominent tech executives including Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. At the center of the scandal is Huang’s affair with Alice Huang of Megaspeed International, a technology company that came under federal scrutiny over suspected efforts to divert advanced Nvidia chips to China. US intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang of having ties to China’s Ministry of State Security, according to published reports. Those allegations remain under investigation, and there has been no public finding that Jensen Huang knowingly shared corporate secrets or helped Beijing evade US export restrictions. Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a November 8 apology to employees but did not identify either woman. sources.title: Nvidia rejects Huang’s return amid SEC probe - Ticker News
passages: Ben Preston of Orbis Global Equity Strategy said the firm sold its Nvidia shares before the latest developments, citing concerns about elevated AI valuations.
He also questioned whether Huang’s return would resolve the broader challenges facing the company.
Nvidia is standing by its leadership decision despite calls for Jensen Huang to return, as a reported US regulatory investigation adds another complication for the technology giant.
However, efforts to bring him back have gained momentum, with Huang reportedly expressing a willingness to return.
The developments come as US lawmakers consider tighter restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, a position Huang has challenged by supporting increased exports.
Meanwhile, the US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over questions about whether investors were misled.
The company has not publicly commented on the matter.
The fallout has also reached the wider AI infrastructure sector, with companies such as CoreWeave, in which Nvidia holds a stake, exposed to shifts in investor sentiment.
In response, Nvidia has established a national security and export oversight committee led by Suzanne Nora Johnson.
The move is intended to strengthen corporate oversight as the company navigates regulatory and geopolitical pressures.
Beyond the leadership dispute, Nvidia faces questions about AI data centre demand and the valuations of companies across the sector.
Huang is also expected to retain considerable influence through his shareholding, which gives him the ability to nominate board members.

The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia following last week’s shock resignation of CEO Jensen Huang amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, sources told The Post on Tuesday. They said the probe will focus on whether Nvidia’s disclosures misled investors — likely examining the company’s denial earlier this year that the fallen tech titan was having an affair with Alice Huang, no relation, of Singapore-based Megaspeed. The ex-Nvidia CEO confessed Nov. 8 to an affair with the woman, an alleged Chinese spy, as reports of affairs with two Nvidia employees surfaced. An SEC spokesperson declined to confirm the probe, telling The Post that the agency “does not comment on the existence or nonexistence of a possible investigation.” Huang signaled Tuesday that he would be willing to reclaim the chief executive job if the company’s board asked him. Nvidia’s directors say that’s not on the table, as The Post reported, despite pressure from employees, prominent investors and tech heavyweights like Elon Musk. Nvidia shares jumped nearly 3% in after-hours trading Tuesday after the chipmaking giant reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings, with adjusted profits of $2.68 a share topping Wall Street estimates of $2.48. Revenue of $115.8 billion also beat forecasts of roughly $109 billion, while the company projected fourth-quarter sales of about $130 billion — ahead of analysts’ expectations of $125 billion. Huang said Tuesday he had been overwhelmed by support from Nvidia employees, investors and business partners urging him to return to the company he co-founded. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics.” The 63-year-old billionaire made clear that he would welcome a comeback — provided Nvidia’s board agreed to reinstate him. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang said. Huang also acknowledged his personal misconduct and pledged to cooperate with an independent investigation commissioned by Nvidia’s directors. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” he said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” He ended the statement with a personal message to his family. “To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.” Nvidia’s board, however, is not considering reinstating Huang despite growing pressure from prominent investors, employees and Silicon Valley heavyweights, according to reports. Nvidia has named longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent replacement for Huang. President Trump weighed in Monday, saying he would support Huang’s return to the helm of the AI chipmaking giant. Musk has also backed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement, joining other prominent tech executives including Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. At the center of the scandal is Huang’s affair with Alice Huang of Megaspeed International, a technology company that came under federal scrutiny over suspected efforts to divert advanced Nvidia chips to China. US intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang of having ties to China’s Ministry of State Security, according to published reports. Those allegations remain under investigation, and there has been no public finding that Jensen Huang knowingly shared corporate secrets or helped Beijing evade US export restrictions. The scandal deepened when the New York Times reported that Huang had also been romantically involved with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reportedly answered directly to the billionaire CEO. The pair were spotted behaving affectionately during Nvidia’s annual developer conference in San Jose in March, according to the Times. Axios separately reported that Huang’s security team allegedly offered a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who recorded an interaction between the two. Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a November 8 apology to employees but did not identify either woman. Nvidia subsequently launched an independent investigation into the allegations, retaining former federal prosecutor Joon H. Kim and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

Nvidia is standing by its leadership decision despite calls for Jensen Huang to return, as a reported US regulatory investigation adds another complication for the technology giant.
However, efforts to bring him back have gained momentum, with Huang reportedly expressing a willingness to return.
The developments come as US lawmakers consider tighter restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, a position Huang has challenged by supporting increased exports.
Meanwhile, the US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over questions about whether investors were misled.
The company has not publicly commented on the matter.
The fallout has also reached the wider AI infrastructure sector, with companies such as CoreWeave, in which Nvidia holds a stake, exposed to shifts in investor sentiment.
In response, Nvidia has established a national security and export oversight committee led by Suzanne Nora Johnson.
The move is intended to strengthen corporate oversight as the company navigates regulatory and geopolitical pressures.
Beyond the leadership dispute, Nvidia faces questions about AI data centre demand and the valuations of companies across the sector.
Huang is also expected to retain considerable influence through his shareholding, which gives him the ability to nominate board members.

extraction.body: Nvidia is standing by its leadership decision despite calls for Jensen Huang to return, as a reported US regulatory investigation adds another complication for the technology giant. The company has dismissed the “Stand With Jensen” movement, which has called for Huang’s reinstatement following his departure. However, efforts to bring him back have gained momentum, with Huang reportedly expressing a willingness to return. Board chair Harvey Jones has maintained that Huang’s departure was voluntary and confirmed there are no plans for him to resume the role. The situation has also drawn attention to Huang’s personal and professional connections, including reported ties to Alice Huang, prompting questions about potential links to Chinese intelligence. The developments come as US lawmakers consider tighter restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, a position Huang has challenged by supporting increased exports. Meanwhile, the US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia over questions about whether investors were misled. The company has not publicly commented on the matter. Although Huang has received support from several influential figures, he has acknowledged that his conduct created difficulties for the board and pledged to cooperate fully. His departure was unanimously accepted by directors. Nvidia shares climbed 4% following the announcement, although analysts described the market response as relatively restrained compared with the company’s financial projections. Rick Meckler of Cherry Lane Investments interpreted the share price increase as investor relief that the situation had not resulted in a more damaging outcome. The fallout has also reached the wider AI infrastructure sector, with companies such as CoreWeave, in which Nvidia holds a stake, exposed to shifts in investor sentiment. In response, Nvidia has established a national security and export oversight committee led by Suzanne Nora Johnson. The move is intended to strengthen corporate oversight as the company navigates regulatory and geopolitical pressures. Huang is also expected to retain considerable influence through his shareholding, which gives him the ability to nominate board members. Beyond the leadership dispute, Nvidia faces questions about AI data centre demand and the valuations of companies across the sector. Ben Preston of Orbis Global Equity Strategy said the firm sold its Nvidia shares before the latest developments, citing concerns about elevated AI valuations. He also questioned whether Huang’s return would resolve the broader challenges facing the company. Nvidia’s governance changes come as the Trump administration weighs further restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips. Technology exports are also expected to feature in discussions between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. For Nvidia, the challenge now is to maintain investor confidence while addressing questions about its leadership, corporate governance and position in an increasingly competitive global AI market. passages: China 's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia 's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission said in a report released Wednesday.

China is making that move as it faces a quality gap between chips produced by Chinese companies, including Huawei and Cambricon , and the more advanced ones produced by Nvidia and other U.S. companies, such as Advanced Micro Devices , the report noted.
The report's findings could fuel concerns about advanced Nvidia chips having found their way to Chinese users amid escalating investigations from Congress and state and federal regulators.

"Although China has made some progress in achieving its goals, it has not yet closed the hardest chokepoints — including the most advanced capabilities in logic fabrication, memory, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, as well as the Nvidia Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) software moat — and likely will not for some time," the report said.

The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was created by Congress in 2000 with a mandate to monitor and report to Congress the national security implications of the trade and economic relationship between the U.S. and China.

extraction.body: China 's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia 's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission said in a report released Wednesday. The report comes as Nvidia has been rocked by the resignation of its CEO, Jensen Huang , after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed , which is being eyed by U.S. investigators for potential diversion of Nvidia's chips to China. "China is seeking to evade U.S. export controls to gain the most advanced semiconductors that underpin its intelligentization drive," the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said in its 2026 annual report to Congress. China is making that move as it faces a quality gap between chips produced by Chinese companies, including Huawei and Cambricon , and the more advanced ones produced by Nvidia and other U.S. companies, such as Advanced Micro Devices , the report noted. The report's findings could fuel concerns about advanced Nvidia chips having found their way to Chinese users amid escalating investigations from Congress and state and federal regulators. "Although China has made some progress in achieving its goals, it has not yet closed the hardest chokepoints — including the most advanced capabilities in logic fabrication, memory, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, as well as the Nvidia Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) software moat — and likely will not for some time," the report said. "The resulting gap in compute is substantial, largely due to U.S. export controls on advanced chips," the report said. The report highlighted the fact that in the meantime, Chinese companies have obtained remote access to Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, including Malaysia. On Tuesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule intended to cut off that workaround. The move came in response to criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Congress members that the Commerce Department had not done enough to prevent Nvidia's most advanced chips from being diverted to China in violation of U.S. export controls. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was created by Congress in 2000 with a mandate to monitor and report to Congress the national security implications of the trade and economic relationship between the U.S. and China. extraction.body: China 's People's Liberation Army has been "actively soliciting" Nvidia 's most advanced semiconductor chips to develop its artificial intelligence-enabled military capabilities, a congressional commission said in a report released Wednesday. The report comes as Nvidia has been rocked by the resignation of its CEO, Jensen Huang , after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed , which is being eyed by U.S. investigators for potential diversion of Nvidia's chips to China. "China is seeking to evade U.S. export controls to gain the most advanced semiconductors that underpin its intelligentization drive," the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said in its 2026 annual report to Congress. China is making that move as it faces a quality gap between chips produced by Chinese companies, including Huawei and Cambricon , and the more advanced ones produced by Nvidia and other U.S. companies, such as Advanced Micro Devices , the report noted. The report's findings could fuel concerns about advanced Nvidia chips having found their way to Chinese users amid escalating investigations from Congress and state and federal regulators. "Although China has made some progress in achieving its goals, it has not yet closed the hardest chokepoints — including the most advanced capabilities in logic fabrication, memory, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, as well as the Nvidia Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) software moat — and likely will not for some time," the report said. "The resulting gap in compute is substantial, largely due to U.S. export controls on advanced chips," the report said. The report highlighted the fact that in the meantime, Chinese companies have obtained remote access to Nvidia chips through data centers in third countries, including Malaysia. On Tuesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued a rule intended to cut off that workaround. The move came in response to criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Congress members that the Commerce Department had not done enough to prevent Nvidia's most advanced chips from being diverted to China in violation of U.S. export controls. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission was created by Congress in 2000 with a mandate to monitor and report to Congress the national security implications of the trade and economic relationship between the U.S. and China. Clarke's decision comes one year after a mistrial in the same case, after jurors failed to agree on whether to convict or acquit former Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) students Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno in this first-of-its-kind scheme, as Reuters first reported . They were also accused of using multiple cryptocurrency addresses and foreign exchanges and setting up shell companies. After the attack, they also allegedly moved the stolen crypto assets through a series of transactions to obscure their source and ownership. The prosecutors also said that, while planning and executing the attack, the brothers deployed a series of "bait transactions" designed to identify "victim traders," exploited a vulnerability in the MEV-Boost relay code, causing the relay to release the full content of a proposed block prematurely, and reordered the proposed block to their advantage. In the next stage of the scheme, they allegedly reordered the block on the Ethereum blockchain, which resulted in the theft of approximately $25 million in cryptocurrency from the victim traders. Throughout the process, the brothers also allegedly searched online for information on carrying out the attack, concealing their involvement in the Ethereum exploit, and laundering the criminal proceeds through cryptocurrency exchanges with lax verification procedures. extraction.body: A U.S. federal judge has acquitted brothers Anton and James Peraire-Bueno of criminal charges stemming from a $25 million Ethereum trading operation that prosecutors alleged was executed in just 12 seconds. A US judge acquitted two MIT-educated brothers in a $25 million Ethereum fraud case. Judge Jessica Clarke ruled that prosecutors failed to establish material misrepresentation. The Ethereum MEV operation generated $25 million in profits within just 12 seconds. The acquittal follows a November 2025 mistrial after jurors failed to reach a verdict. Flashbots patched its relay software within 24 hours of the April 2023 MEV incident. Clarke ruled that prosecutors had failed to establish a material misrepresentation, an essential element of wire fraud. The decision clears the Massachusetts Institute of Technology-educated brothers of wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering. Their trial ended in a mistrial in November 2025 after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict. US judge finds no material deception in Ethereum trading case Much of Clarke's ruling examined the rules governing Ethereum and whether participants make explicit or implicit promises when submitting transactions, registering validators or interacting with software used to organize blockchain transactions. “It is a trustless, highly adversarial environment with no terms of use,” Clarke wrote, describing Ethereum. Federal prosecutors argued that the brothers' trading activity involved deception because they deliberately placed transactions designed to attract automated trading bots before disrupting the bots' intended trades. Clarke rejected the argument that submitting a transaction to Ethereum's public pool of pending transactions amounted to an agreement that it would be executed alongside other trades in a particular order. The judge found that the government's comparison with spoofing in traditional financial markets was equally problematic. Unlike orders placed with the intention of canceling them, the brothers' bait transactions were never withdrawn and appeared on the blockchain within approximately one minute of the operation. Neither Ethereum nor the MEV-Boost software specifications established the obligations that prosecutors claimed the brothers had violated, the ruling said. How the brothers made $25 million from Ethereum trading bots At the center of the prosecution was a trading operation called Omakase, which targeted cryptocurrency traders engaged in a practice known as sandwich trading. Court records show that the Peraire-Bueno brothers spent months preparing Omakase and registered 16 Ethereum validators capable of facilitating the operation. In April 2023, eight transactions attracted sandwich traders whose automated programs assembled trades intended to profit from the brothers' purchases. Using that information, the brothers altered the proposed arrangement of transactions, disrupting the sandwich traders' expected sales and generating approximately $25 million in profits. The brothers' validator incurred a penalty of 1 ETH for proposing two blocks during the same Ethereum block production slot. Court rejects prosecution's arguments over MEV-Boost software Another part of the government's case concerned invalid information contained in a digitally signed block header submitted to the Ultrasound Relay during Omakase. Clarke acknowledged that the information was incorrect, but trial evidence established that the relay did not examine the disputed fields before releasing the block's transaction data. The purportedly false information consequently “had no impact on the behavior of its recipient,” the judge wrote. Prosecutors did not present an expert witness on Ethereum's trading environment or call a representative from Ultrasound during the trial. Clarke cited the separate 2025 wire fraud ruling involving Mango Markets trader Avraham Eisenberg, where the court found that other users' expectations about the operation of a cryptocurrency platform did not establish that the defendant had made a false promise. Ethereum prosecution ends more than two years after arrests As crypto.news previously reported, U.S. authorities arrested the brothers in May 2024 following an investigation involving the Internal Revenue Service's Criminal Investigation unit. In July 2025, Clarke rejected an earlier motion to dismiss the fraud charges, although a separate charge of conspiracy to receive stolen property was dismissed after prosecutors decided not to pursue it. The November 2026 ruling found that the evidence presented at trial could not sustain the wire fraud charges. The money laundering conspiracy charge depended on the proceeds of the alleged fraud and therefore failed as well. Court records show that Flashbots temporarily blacklisted the validator involved in Omakase and updated its relay software within 24 hours of the incident. A cryptocurrency wallet containing $3 million of the proceeds was frozen, while the brothers had converted their remaining profits into U.S. dollars by October 2023.

extraction.body: A pair of computer programmers accused of exploiting a software bug to steal millions of dollars in just 12 seconds have been acquitted of wire fraud charges. The US has failed in its efforts to convince a district court that two brothers who allegedly stole $25 million in cryptocurrency by exploiting the Ethereum blockchain are guilty of wire fraud and money laundering . Handing down its decision on Monday (16 November), the US District Court for the Southern District of New York acquitted Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno on three charges , holding that the government had failed to prove that the pair had made any material misrepresentations upon which a finding of wire fraud – and consequently, money laundering – rested. US District Judge Jessica Clarke made clear that the case did not centre on whether the brothers’ conduct was “improper, objectionable or even despicable”. The issue at hand was solely whether the pair had committed wire fraud. The Peraire-Bueno brothers were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud , wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering in May 2024 over their involvement in an alleged scheme to fraudulently obtain approximately $25 million in a matter of seconds from cryptocurrency traders. The exploit was said to be the very first of its kind. According to the government, the Peraire-Buenos’ ‘Omakase’ scheme targeted sandwich traders – who profit off the manipulated inflation of a token’s value – on the blockchain platform Ethereum. Through ‘lure transactions’, the brothers are said to have enticed traders’ bots to trade away millions of dollars in cryptocurrency that would usually be made back, with a small profit. However, the Peraire-Buenos allegedly exploited a coding vulnerability that allowed them to view private transactions and propose their own replacement transactions that disrupted the traders’ strategy. The sandwich traders lost millions in seconds, the government said, while the Peraire-Buenos reaped “significant profits”. A mistrial was declared in November 2025 after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. Before the district court was a motion for acquittal or, alternatively, dismissal of the superseding indictment. A finding that an individual violated the wire fraud statute requires proof that they devised, or else intended to devise, a scheme to obtain money or property “by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations or promises”. Proving the existence of a scheme to defraud requires the government to prove that the “misrepresentations were material and that the defendant acted with fraudulent intent”. Judge Clarke said that the evidence at trial “could arguably show that the Peraire-Buenos concocted a scheme to obtain cryptocurrency from sandwich traders on Ethereum”. Yet the government ultimately failed to propose a theory that would lead a reasonable juror to infer that the brothers had conveyed a material misrepresentation through the scheme. The judge held that none of the three key features of Omakase – the lure transactions, the submission of a false digital signature and the failure to act in accordance with the software’s specifications – could be considered a material representation by the Peraire-Buenos. She also rejected the “government’s repeat attempts to rid the court of its obligation find a material misrepresentation”. The superseding indictment had charged the Peraire-Buenos with conspiracy to launder the proceeds of wire fraud, meaning the money laundering charge fell with the wire fraud. Judge Clarke concluded that “no reasonable juror applying the law could find the Peraire-Buenos guilty of conspiracy to commit money laundering”, emphasising that the jury had been instructed to find that the financial transactions involved wire fraud proceeds. Finding that the government had failed to prove material misrepresentations by the Peraire-Buenos, the court acquitted the pair. Never miss a story — set ICLG as a preferred source on Google

coreStoryFacts.text: US District Judge Jessica Clarke has acquitted two brothers accused of stealing $25 million in cryptocurrency in about 12 seconds through a scheme that exploited a bug in the Ethereum blockchain.
"The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos' conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.
It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case," the federal judge said .
A US judge acquitted two MIT-educated brothers in a $25 million Ethereum fraud case.

US judge finds no material deception in Ethereum trading case Much of Clarke's ruling examined the rules governing Ethereum and whether participants make explicit or implicit promises when submitting transactions, registering validators or interacting with software used to organize blockchain transactions.
The Ethereum MEV operation generated $25 million in profits within just 12 seconds.

Ethereum prosecution ends more than two years after arrests As crypto.news previously reported, U.S. authorities arrested the brothers in May 2024 following an investigation involving the Internal Revenue Service's Criminal Investigation unit.
Court records show that the Peraire-Bueno brothers spent months preparing Omakase and registered 16 Ethereum validators capable of facilitating the operation.
The brothers' validator incurred a penalty of 1 ETH for proposing two blocks during the same Ethereum block production slot.
“It is a trustless, highly adversarial environment with no terms of use,” Clarke wrote, describing Ethereum.

Clarke rejected the argument that submitting a transaction to Ethereum's public pool of pending transactions amounted to an agreement that it would be executed alongside other trades in a particular order.
Neither Ethereum nor the MEV-Boost software specifications established the obligations that prosecutors claimed the brothers had violated, the ruling said.
Prosecutors did not present an expert witness on Ethereum's trading environment or call a representative from Ultrasound during the trial.
The decision clears the Massachusetts Institute of Technology-educated brothers of wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering.

Federal prosecutors argued that the brothers' trading activity involved deception because they deliberately placed transactions designed to attract automated trading bots before disrupting the bots' intended trades.

The November 2026 ruling found that the evidence presented at trial could not sustain the wire fraud charges. The money laundering conspiracy charge depended on the proceeds of the alleged fraud and therefore failed as well. Court records show that Flashbots temporarily blacklisted the validator involved in Omakase and updated its relay software within 24 hours of the incident. A cryptocurrency wallet containing $3 million of the proceeds was frozen, while the brothers had converted their remaining profits into U.S. dollars by October 2023.

extraction.body: A pair of computer programmers accused of exploiting a software bug to steal millions of dollars in just 12 seconds have been acquitted of wire fraud charges. The US has failed in its efforts to convince a district court that two brothers who allegedly stole $25 million in cryptocurrency by exploiting the Ethereum blockchain are guilty of wire fraud and money laundering . Handing down its decision on Monday (16 November), the US District Court for the Southern District of New York acquitted Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno on three charges , holding that the government had failed to prove that the pair had made any material misrepresentations upon which a finding of wire fraud – and consequently, money laundering – rested. US District Judge Jessica Clarke made clear that the case did not centre on whether the brothers’ conduct was “improper, objectionable or even despicable”. The issue at hand was solely whether the pair had committed wire fraud. The Peraire-Bueno brothers were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud , wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering in May 2024 over their involvement in an alleged scheme to fraudulently obtain approximately $25 million in a matter of seconds from cryptocurrency traders. The exploit was said to be the very first of its kind. According to the government, the Peraire-Buenos’ ‘Omakase’ scheme targeted sandwich traders – who profit off the manipulated inflation of a token’s value – on the blockchain platform Ethereum. Through ‘lure transactions’, the brothers are said to have enticed traders’ bots to trade away millions of dollars in cryptocurrency that would usually be made back, with a small profit. However, the Peraire-Buenos allegedly exploited a coding vulnerability that allowed them to view private transactions and propose their own replacement transactions that disrupted the traders’ strategy. The sandwich traders lost millions in seconds, the government said, while the Peraire-Buenos reaped “significant profits”. A mistrial was declared in November 2025 after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict. Before the district court was a motion for acquittal or, alternatively, dismissal of the superseding indictment. A finding that an individual violated the wire fraud statute requires proof that they devised, or else intended to devise, a scheme to obtain money or property “by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations or promises”. Proving the existence of a scheme to defraud requires the government to prove that the “misrepresentations were material and that the defendant acted with fraudulent intent”. Judge Clarke said that the evidence at trial “could arguably show that the Peraire-Buenos concocted a scheme to obtain cryptocurrency from sandwich traders on Ethereum”. Yet the government ultimately failed to propose a theory that would lead a reasonable juror to infer that the brothers had conveyed a material misrepresentation through the scheme. The judge held that none of the three key features of Omakase – the lure transactions, the submission of a false digital signature and the failure to act in accordance with the software’s specifications – could be considered a material representation by the Peraire-Buenos. She also rejected the “government’s repeat attempts to rid the court of its obligation find a material misrepresentation”. The superseding indictment had charged the Peraire-Buenos with conspiracy to launder the proceeds of wire fraud, meaning the money laundering charge fell with the wire fraud. Judge Clarke concluded that “no reasonable juror applying the law could find the Peraire-Buenos guilty of conspiracy to commit money laundering”, emphasising that the jury had been instructed to find that the financial transactions involved wire fraud proceeds. Finding that the government had failed to prove material misrepresentations by the Peraire-Buenos, the court acquitted the pair. Never miss a story — set ICLG as a preferred source on Google

sources.title: Nvidia stops shipping US-approved AI chips to China
passages: SHENZHEN, China, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Nvidia has stopped shipping powerful artificial intelligence chips to China, its interim CEO said, raising doubts about the future of a special licensing agreement negotiated by Washington and Beijing.
"Our guidance does not have any licenced Hopper data centre products included, and we are no longer shipping licenced Hopper data centre products to China," Kress said.
And the China export arrangement also imposed a 25% tariff on eligible chips imported into the United States before shipment to China.
TRUMP EASED EXPORT CURBS AFTER XI SUMMIT, HUANG LOBBYING The US introduced export controls on the chips in 2022 and subsequently tightened China's access to them.
Reuters reported earlier this month that around 600,000 H200 chips were being stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China after Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports.
She did not explain why Nvidia had stopped shipping the processors or whether the halt would be permanent.
H200 chips are manufactured for Nvidia in Taiwan by TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker.
That decision followed months of lobbying from Huang, who stepped down as he faced allegations he had extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.

extraction.body: SHENZHEN, China, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Nvidia has stopped shipping powerful artificial intelligence chips to China, its interim CEO said, raising doubts about the future of a special licensing agreement negotiated by Washington and Beijing. Colette Kress, who replaced Jensen Huang following his resignation last week, said during an earnings call on Tuesday that the US chipmaker sold $2.4 billion worth of licensed Hopper-generation data centre products to China in the quarter ended October 25. But she said there were no current plans for further shipments. "Our guidance does not have any licenced Hopper data centre products included, and we are no longer shipping licenced Hopper data centre products to China," Kress said. She did not explain why Nvidia had stopped shipping the processors or whether the halt would be permanent. The Hopper family includes the H200, a powerful processor used to train and run advanced AI models. TRUMP EASED EXPORT CURBS AFTER XI SUMMIT, HUANG LOBBYING The US introduced export controls on the chips in 2022 and subsequently tightened China's access to them. Following a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping last year, however, US President Donald Trump said he would allow H200 sales to approved Chinese customers. The US eased its licensing policy for the H200 in January, allowing export applications to be reviewed individually subject to security conditions. That decision followed months of lobbying from Huang, who stepped down as he faced allegations he had extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees. H200 chips are manufactured for Nvidia in Taiwan by TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker. And the China export arrangement also imposed a 25% tariff on eligible chips imported into the United States before shipment to China. Washington approved H200 sales to 10 Chinese companies, including Alibaba, Tencent and TikTok owner ByteDance, according to previous Reuters reporting. Reuters reported earlier this month that around 600,000 H200 chips were being stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China after Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports. Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips in recent months, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. (Reporting by Eduardo Baptista in Shenzhen; Editing by Joe Bavier) By Eduardo Baptista

The development was confirmed by Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday. She said the company had no plans to make further shipments of licensed Hopper-generation data centre products to China.

Kress took over as interim CEO following Jensen Huang’s resignation last week. Her announcement has raised concerns about the future of Nvidia’s business in China, particularly as both countries continue to navigate restrictions on advanced semiconductor technology.

However, she made it clear that the company’s latest financial guidance does not include any further shipments of these products to the Chinese market.
“Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data centre products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data centre products to China,” Kress said.
She did not provide a specific reason for the decision or clarify whether the suspension of shipments would be permanent.
Nvidia’s Hopper series includes some of the company’s powerful processors designed for artificial intelligence and data centre operations.
One of the key products in this range is the H200 chip, which is used to train and run advanced AI models.

These processors play an important role in handling the large amounts of computing power required for AI development. They are used by companies and research organisations to build and operate advanced AI systems.
Nvidia’s decision to stop shipments could therefore have implications for Chinese companies looking to access advanced computing hardware for their AI development.
The announcement has also raised questions about a special licensing arrangement negotiated between Washington and Beijing.
The agreement was expected to provide a way for Nvidia to sell certain advanced AI chips to Chinese customers under US licensing conditions.
However, with the company now confirming that it has stopped shipping licensed Hopper products to China, the future of these sales remains uncertain.
Nvidia has not explained whether the decision is linked to regulatory restrictions, business considerations or other factors.
